planner-fingerprint.sql:
select true as ok,
       (waiting.n > 0) as blocked,
       'ap=' || coalesce(to_char((select max(p.updated_at) from public.assignment_progress p) at time zone 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS.US"Z"'), 'none')
       || ',rp=' || coalesce(to_char((select max(q.updated_at) from public.reading_progress q) at time zone 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS.US"Z"'), 'none')
       || ',n=' || (select count(*) from public.assignments a)::text
       || ',apn=' || (select count(*) from public.assignment_progress p)::text
       || ',rpn=' || (select count(*) from public.reading_progress q)::text
       || ',at=' || to_char(now() at time zone 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS.US"Z"') as fingerprint,
       waiting.n as requests_open_now, waiting.first_id as first_open_request_id, stale.n as stale_claims,
       r.id as newest_request_id, r.kind as newest_request_kind, r.state as newest_request_state,
       r.created_at as newest_request_created_at, r.claimed_at as newest_request_claimed_at,
       r.finished_at as newest_request_finished_at
  from (select count(*)::integer as n, min(g.id) as first_id
          from public.agent_requests g
         where g.state in ('queued', 'claimed')
           and coalesce(g.claimed_at, g.created_at) >= now() - interval '6 hours') waiting
 cross join (select count(*)::integer as n
               from public.agent_requests g
              where g.state in ('queued', 'claimed')
                and coalesce(g.claimed_at, g.created_at) < now() - interval '6 hours') stale
  left join lateral (select g.id, g.kind, g.state, g.created_at, g.claimed_at, g.finished_at
                       from public.agent_requests g
                      order by g.id desc
                      limit 1) r on true
planner-fingerprint.expect: One row: a reading, with one check. fingerprint holds, as one string, the newest assignment_progress and reading_progress change, the count of assignments, the count of assignment_progress rows (apn), the count of reading_progress rows (rpn) and the time of this read. blocked when an agent_requests row is queued or claimed now (filed or taken within the last 6 hours): a sync or an Inbox apply is waiting or running, so the run stops here, before it has stopped a container or spent a question, and is repeated once that request has ended. A request left queued or claimed for more than 6 hours is not a running sync: it blocks nothing and is counted in stale_claims. The last columns are the newest agent_requests row.

planner-unchanged.sql:
with given as (
  select substring($1::text from '^(.*),at=') as planner,
         substring($1::text from ',at=(.*)$')::timestamptz as since
), seen as (
  select 'ap=' || coalesce(to_char((select max(p.updated_at) from public.assignment_progress p) at time zone 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS.US"Z"'), 'none')
       || ',rp=' || coalesce(to_char((select max(q.updated_at) from public.reading_progress q) at time zone 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS.US"Z"'), 'none')
       || ',n=' || (select count(*) from public.assignments a)::text
       || ',apn=' || (select count(*) from public.assignment_progress p)::text
       || ',rpn=' || (select count(*) from public.reading_progress q)::text as planner
), moved as (
  select count(*)::integer as n, min(g.id) as first_id, max(g.id) as last_id
    from public.agent_requests g, given
   where g.created_at >= given.since or g.claimed_at >= given.since or g.finished_at >= given.since
), running as (
  select count(*)::integer as n, min(g.id) as first_id
    from public.agent_requests g
   where g.state = 'claimed' and g.claimed_at >= now() - interval '6 hours'
), stale as (
  select count(*)::integer as n
    from public.agent_requests g
   where g.state = 'claimed' and g.claimed_at < now() - interval '6 hours'
)
select (seen.planner = given.planner) as ok,
       (seen.planner <> given.planner and (moved.n > 0 or running.n > 0)) as blocked,
       $1::text as planner_before,
       seen.planner || ',at=' || to_char(now() at time zone 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS.US"Z"') as planner_now,
       given.since as since, now() as read_at,
       moved.n as requests_in_window, moved.first_id as first_request_id, moved.last_id as last_request_id,
       running.n as requests_claimed_now, running.first_id as first_claimed_request_id, stale.n as stale_claims
  from given, seen, moved, running, stale
planner-unchanged.expect: One row. ok when the five planner values read the same as in the fingerprint: a row changed, added or deleted in assignment_progress or reading_progress, or an assignment added or removed, makes them differ. A planner that reads the same passes whatever else ran: what did not change was changed by nobody. blocked only when the values differ AND a sync or an Inbox apply could be why: an agent_requests row was created, claimed or finished at or after the time the fingerprint was read, or one was claimed within the last 6 hours and has not ended. Then the change cannot be laid at the Workspace and the run is repeated. A claim older than 6 hours is not a running sync (stale_claims counts them) and does not turn a failure into a repeat.

turn.sql:
select (r.state = 'done' and r.error_code is null
        and r.created_at >= $3::timestamptz - interval '60 seconds'
        and u.id is not null and md5(u.content) = $4::text
        and ($7::bigint is null or r.id > $7::bigint)
        and m.id is not null and m.tier = $2::text and m.provider = 'claude-cli'
        and m.finished and m.error_code is null
        and ($6::text is null or $5::text is not null)
        and ($5::text is null
             or m.tool_calls @> jsonb_build_array(
                  jsonb_strip_nulls(jsonb_build_object('tool', $5::text, 'scope', $6::text, 'ok', true))))) as ok,
       r.id as request_id, r.state as request_state, r.error_code as request_error_code, r.conversation_id,
       r.created_at, r.claimed_at, r.finished_at,
       $3::timestamptz as run_started_at,
       (r.created_at >= $3::timestamptz - interval '60 seconds') as asked_in_this_run,
       (md5(u.content) = $4::text) as question_matches,
       m.id as message_id, m.tier, m.provider, m.model, m.finished, m.error_code as message_error_code,
       (select coalesce(jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object('tool', e.value->>'tool', 'scope', e.value->>'scope', 'ok', e.value->'ok')
                                  order by e.ordinality), '[]'::jsonb)
          from jsonb_array_elements(m.tool_calls) with ordinality e) as tools,
       ($7::bigint is null or r.id > $7::bigint) as asked_after_earlier
  from public.workspace_requests r
  left join public.workspace_messages u on u.id = r.user_message_id and u.role = 'user'
  left join public.workspace_messages m on m.request_id = r.id and m.role = 'assistant'
 where r.id = $1::bigint
turn.expect: One row. ok when the request is this run's (created no earlier than 60 seconds before the run started), its question is the one the step asks (the md5 of the user message's text is the md5 given), it was asked after the step before it (when the request of that step is given as "after", this request is the later one, so one request cannot stand for two steps), it is done with no error code, and its answer was written at the given tier by provider claude-cli, is finished with no error code, and (when a tool is given) its tool calls hold that tool, with that scope when one is given, marked ok.

turn-stopped.sql:
select (r.state = 'cancelled' and r.error_code = 'cancelled'
        and r.created_at >= $2::timestamptz - interval '60 seconds'
        and u.id is not null and md5(u.content) = $3::text
        and ($4::bigint is null or r.id > $4::bigint)
        and r.claimed_at is not null
        and m.id is not null and m.finished and m.error_code = 'cancelled') as ok,
       r.id as request_id, r.state as request_state, r.error_code as request_error_code, r.conversation_id,
       r.created_at, r.claimed_at, r.finished_at,
       $2::timestamptz as run_started_at,
       (r.created_at >= $2::timestamptz - interval '60 seconds') as asked_in_this_run,
       (md5(u.content) = $3::text) as question_matches,
       (r.claimed_at is not null) as runner_took_it,
       m.id as message_id, m.tier, m.finished, m.error_code as message_error_code,
       ($4::bigint is null or r.id > $4::bigint) as asked_after_earlier
  from public.workspace_requests r
  left join public.workspace_messages u on u.id = r.user_message_id and u.role = 'user'
  left join public.workspace_messages m on m.request_id = r.id and m.role = 'assistant'
 where r.id = $1::bigint
turn-stopped.expect: One row. ok when the request is this run's (created no earlier than 60 seconds before the run started), its question is the one the step asks (the md5 of the user message's text is the md5 given), it was asked after the step before it (when the request of that step is given as "after", this request is the later one), it is cancelled with the code cancelled, the runner had taken it, and its answer is there and is finished with the code cancelled: it was stopped part-way. A question cancelled while it still waited has no claim and no answer, is a row the page's own login can make without the runner, and does not pass.

turn-waiting.sql:
select (r.state = 'queued' and r.claimed_at is null and r.finished_at is null and r.error_code is null
        and r.created_at >= $2::timestamptz - interval '60 seconds'
        and u.id is not null and md5(u.content) = $3::text) as ok,
       r.id as request_id, r.state as request_state, r.error_code as request_error_code, r.conversation_id,
       r.created_at, r.claimed_at, r.finished_at,
       $2::timestamptz as run_started_at,
       (r.created_at >= $2::timestamptz - interval '60 seconds') as asked_in_this_run,
       (md5(u.content) = $3::text) as question_matches,
       floor(extract(epoch from (now() - r.created_at)))::integer as waited_s
  from public.workspace_requests r
  left join public.workspace_messages u on u.id = r.user_message_id and u.role = 'user'
 where r.id = $1::bigint
turn-waiting.expect: One row. ok when the request is this run's (created no earlier than 60 seconds before the run started), its question is the one the step asked (the md5 of the user message's text is the md5 given), and it is in the queue now: state queued, taken by nobody, not ended, no error code. It is read while the Workspace service is still stopped, so it shows that a question asked then waits and does not expire. waited_s is how long it has waited so far, by the database's clock.

turn-answered-after.sql:
select (r.state = 'done' and r.error_code is null
        and r.created_at >= $2::timestamptz - interval '60 seconds'
        and r.claimed_at >= r.created_at + make_interval(secs => $3::integer)
        and u.id is not null and md5(u.content) = $4::text
        and m.id is not null and m.finished and m.error_code is null) as ok,
       r.id as request_id, r.state as request_state, r.error_code as request_error_code, r.conversation_id,
       r.created_at, r.claimed_at, r.finished_at,
       $2::timestamptz as run_started_at,
       (r.created_at >= $2::timestamptz - interval '60 seconds') as asked_in_this_run,
       (md5(u.content) = $4::text) as question_matches,
       $3::integer as min_wait_s,
       floor(extract(epoch from (r.claimed_at - r.created_at)))::integer as waited_s,
       m.id as message_id, m.tier, m.finished, m.error_code as message_error_code
  from public.workspace_requests r
  left join public.workspace_messages u on u.id = r.user_message_id and u.role = 'user'
  left join public.workspace_messages m on m.request_id = r.id and m.role = 'assistant'
 where r.id = $1::bigint
turn-answered-after.expect: One row. ok when the request is this run's (created no earlier than 60 seconds before the run started), its question is the one the step asked (the md5 of the user message's text is the md5 given), is done with no error code, was claimed at least the given number of seconds after it was created, and its answer is finished with no error code: a question that waited while the service was stopped was answered once it came back. Both times are the database's own; no clock of a sandbox is compared.

spike-archived.sql:
select (count(*) filter (where c.archived) = 1 and count(*) filter (where not c.archived) = 0) as ok,
       (count(*) filter (where c.archived))::integer as archived,
       (count(*) filter (where not c.archived))::integer as listed
  from public.workspace_conversations c
 where c.title = 'spike'
spike-archived.expect: One row. ok when exactly one conversation titled 'spike' is archived and none is still listed.

conversations-archived.sql:
with wanted as (
  select unnest($1::uuid[]) as id
)
select (count(*) > 0 and count(*) = count(c.id) and count(*) = count(*) filter (where c.archived)
        and count(*) = count(*) filter (where c.created_at >= $2::timestamptz - interval '60 seconds')) as ok,
       count(*)::integer as asked_for,
       count(c.id)::integer as found,
       (count(*) filter (where c.archived))::integer as archived,
       (count(*) filter (where c.created_at >= $2::timestamptz - interval '60 seconds'))::integer as made_in_this_run,
       coalesce(array_agg(w.id) filter (where c.id is null or not c.archived), '{}') as not_archived
  from wanted w
  left join public.workspace_conversations c on c.id = w.id
conversations-archived.expect: One row. ok when every conversation named exists, is archived, and is this run's (created no earlier than 60 seconds before the run started); not_archived lists the ids that are missing or still listed.
